task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: ReadableStream and TransformStream mailbox on the main thread

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from adjusted character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The rs_-prefixed relay proof is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The live reducer configuration is selected only after field-journal capture, pointer gesture authorization, asynchronous stream framing and route-graph fan-in.
The target path requires request-control edits, scope and nonce clicks, then a pointer hold exceeding the authorization threshold.

After pointer release, the path crosses capability resolution, gesture gating, tuple construction, Web Crypto and idle scheduling, ReadableStream framing, a TransformStream mailbox, three route branches, graph fan-in, config materialization, signature derivation, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same authorized hold emits non-target preview/audit objects carrying request_sig-like values, while the bundle also contains an ap_-prefixed proof constructor and vendor-like decoys.
The target value is separated from pointer release by SubtleCrypto, requestIdleCallback, Promise aggregation, ReadableStream and TransformStream boundaries.
Independent gesture, journal and policy branches are merged before a WeakMap-backed runtime configuration is materialized.
The final sink receives an already derived request signature after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: signature-like long-hold-authorized relay request proof token
behavior_category.reason: The observable request_sig is an rs_-prefixed deterministic proof token derived from relay request controls, a field journal, an authorized pointer gesture, capability state and route-graph/runtime configuration. It behaves like a client-side request signature even though this local benchmark does not issue a network request.

near_categories.why_not: Journal and gesture state are inputs, but the observable is explicitly a relay request proof token rather than a reusable UI-state snapshot.
No request body is rewritten or emitted; the requested observable is the derived proof token.
Pointer and DOM runtime state influence config selection, but the target behavior is relay request proof derivation rather than browser identity collection.

construct_validity.note: Obfuscation is asymmetric: identifierNamesGenerator='mangled' with renameGlobals=false keeps top-level function names (including the anchor and several helpers/decoys) readable in the bundle, which is required so the agent can submit answer_function from captures. A case-insensitive keyword search (e.g. 'signature'/'derive'/'request_sig') can therefore narrow candidates to a small readable set. The intended core difficulty is consequently the semantic disambiguation within that small set (anchor vs nested helper vs core utility vs path/wrapper vs off-chain decoy, including the ap_-prefixed proof decoy and the preview/audit objects) rather than long-chain call-depth tracking alone. The declared call_depth/async/control-flow numbers describe the runtime path that produces the value, not the only barrier to locating it.
